On Jun 27, 2023, at 7:52 AM, QuotaGuard Team <notify@quotaguard.com> wrote:

Getting Started With QuotaGuard.com

Hi,
First of all, welcome to QuotaGuard Static, we're happy you've decided to try out our service for your n2n-canvassing-server application. This email should get you up and running in no time.
Please keep this email for future reference, as it can help with setting up, reaching out to support, knowing your configurations, and answering general FAQ.
Note: Provisioning the QuotaGuard Add-On does not automatically route your application traffic through the QuotaGuard Static IP’s. There are a few steps to setup your app to send only desired traffic through the Static IP’s, as outlined below.

Accessing Static IP Connection Settings

You can start using our service immediately using the credentials we added to your dyno in the QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL environment variable.
Additionally, your Static IP connection information can be found in your QuotaGuard administrator dashboard.
To reach the dashboard, either run $ heroku addons:open quotaguardstatic or click on the upper right arrow next to the QuotaGuard Add­on. If you have trouble finding it, please follow Step 6 from the instructions in this blog post, How to Provision the QuotaGuard Add-on.

Your Static IPs

  • 34.232.217.139
  • 18.213.181.255
Please allow all IP addresses for any whitelisting or firewall rules, as traffic may route through any of the IP addresses at any time.

Subscription Information

Username: xvg4wmoayjo9bo
Proxy Password: Located in your dashboard

Connection Strings

HTTP url: http://xvg4wmoayjo9bo:{PASSWORD}@us-east-static-10.quotaguard.com:9293(for HTTP and HTTPS traffic)
SOCKS url: socks5://xvg4wmoayjo9bo:{PASSWORD}@us-east-static-10.quotaguard.com:1080 (for all types of TCP traffic)

Testing Your Connection

via Heroku CLI

$ heroku run 'curl -x http://xvg4wmoayjo9bo:{PASSWORD}@us-east-static-10.quotaguard.com:9293 -L ip.quotaguard.com'

via Curl

$ curl -x http://xvg4wmoayjo9bo:{PASSWORD}@us-east-static-10.quotaguard.com:9293 -L ip.quotaguard.com

Inbound Proxy

If you are looking to use the inbound proxy, you will need to upgrade to the Micro plan or higher. To upgrade you either run $ heroku addons:upgrade quotaguardstatic:micro or change the plan from the Resource tab on the heroku dashboard.
Setup instructions for Inbound Proxys can be found at Getting Started with QuotaGuard Statics IP Inbound Proxy.

Support

To access support and get help, we have a few options for you, or you can just open a new ticket at our Support portal and we will answer you directly.
  • Heroku Documentation for QuotaGuard Static.
  • Setup Support for configuring with Node.js, Ruby, Python, Go, Java, and PHP, etc.
  • Setup QuotaGuard for MongoDB
  • Need to Create a Support Ticket?
  • News and Announcements? Find them at our Blog
  • Request for Dedicated Proxy Setup (Enterprise plans and higher)
  • Do you have Privacy, GDPR, or Legal Questions?
Thanks for giving us a try and don't be shy about reaching out for help, we're always here to assist with any questions you might have.
Michael
QuotaGuard Static
P.S. If you are working with sensitive data like HIPAA, Financial, or Personally Identifiable Information (PII), you will want to check out QuotaGuard Shield. It's the same as QuotaGuard Static but with stronger end to end security for your requests.

Share How You Found Us

We are always interested to learn how you came to subscribe to QuotaGuard Static. If you don’t mind, we would love to hear about how you found our service. Just reply to this email, tell us where you heard about QuotaGuard.

subject: [Inquiry regarding Calling QuotaGuard from Heroku using Java]
description:
Hi there,
This is Janet and I'm currently in charge of Philip Morris Korea's Heroku maintenance.
 
I am writing an email to get help on making API callouts from Heroku Java application to external service via the QuotaGuard system.
My current codes are as follows.

String response = HttpUtil.callParamHttpProxyURLConnection(url, "GET", requestPropMap, paramsMap, charsetString);

public static String callParamHttpProxyURLConnection(String apiUrl, String requestMethod, Map<String, String> requestPropMap, Map<String, String> params, String charsetType)  throws IOException {
          URL proxyUrl = new URL(System.getenv("QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL"));

         String user = userInfo.substring(0, userInfo.indexOf(':'));
         String password = userInfo.substring(userInfo.indexOf(':') + 1);
         System.setProperty("http.proxyHost", proxyUrl.getHost());
         System.setProperty("http.proxyPort", Integer.toString(proxyUrl.getPort()));
         System.setProperty("https.proxyHost", proxyUrl.getHost());
         System.setProperty("https.proxyPort", Integer.toString(proxyUrl.getPort()));  
         System.setProperty("jdk.http.auth.tunneling.disabledSchemes", "");

         Authenticator.setDefault(new Authenticator() {
             protected PasswordAuthentication getPasswordAuthentication() {
                 return new PasswordAuthentication(user, password.toCharArray());
             }
         });

         String result = callParamHttpURLConnection(apiUrl, requestMethod, requestPropMap, params, charsetType);
       
        return result;
    }

    And this code returns the following error message.
HTTP Response Header : {null=[HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required], Proxy-Authenticate=[Basic realm=Basic], Content-Length=[33]}

In fact, the same error message occurred in my staging server and after I added setProperty and cleared tunneling schemes, it worked in my staging server.
However, after the same codes were deployed to my prod server, it returned a 407 error.

As I observed, It seems that I'm unable to call Quotaguard itself from my Heroku app.
When I check up on QuotaGuard Dashboard, there are no logs of callouts.
But the weird thing is that it works from my local computer.
After changing the proxy callout codes below, when I debugged from the local computer, it returned 200 and the log was stacked properly.
//local Test
        //  URL proxyUrl = new URL("http://[Id]:[Password]@[host]:[port]");
           
// String user = "[Id]";
            // String password = "[password]";
            // System.setProperty("http.proxyHost", "[host]");
            // System.setProperty("http.proxyPort", Integer.[port]);        
            // System.setProperty("https.proxyHost", "[host]");
            // System.setProperty("https.proxyPort", Integer.[port]);      
            // System.setProperty("jdk.http.auth.tunneling.disabledSchemes", "");  

I wonder how this could be resolved.
When calling out QuotaGuard (proxying through QG), do we need any tunneling ips allowed?
Currently, there are no tunnels created in my prod server whereas there are 2 tunnels created in my staging server.
Could this lack of tunnel be the cause of 407 error?

Hope to hear back from you soon and Thanks for your help in advance.

Regards,
Janet

How does ssl work for imap while using a proxy?

Maybe I'm doing this the completely wrong way? How would you recommend to proxy IMAP traffic, but only for specific IP destinations, using a ruby on rails application hosted on Heroku?

Thanks in advance!

Wolfram.

To confirm, are the static IPs with base /32 cidr notation? Additionally, we are also receiving in our application logs the following error:

2023-05-25T15:00:03.761912+00:00 app[web.1]: 2023/05/25 10:00:03 Starting listener on 127.0.0.1:50432 for xx.xxx.xx.xx:xxxxx

How can we get past this error? Please advise.
description_text:
Hello,

description:
Hi!

We have a customer who needs to SFTP from their system (OMNICMS) to us (Pantheon). and they are running into 3 issues:

1) Omni's configuration only allows for port 21/22 (Pantheon's SFTP port is 2222)
2) That system can't store usernames longer than 32 characters (Pantheon's are 40 characters)
3) Omni can't be configured to use proxy settings.

So given all of that, Is there a way to set quotaguard up to receive on port 21/22 inbound, and connect to pantheon on 2222? and, for extra points, is there a way for quotaguard to store the pantheon credentials, and have OMNI connect using different credentials that are sized appropriately?

Worth noting, If this is something that can be done, we will be getting a lot of customers who want to use us to host their Omni sites, so this could be quite a bit larger than just one customer doing this one time.

Thanks in advance for your help!
-Chris Porter

Hello Michael, thank you for reaching out.

The reason why we are looking into using QuotaGuard is that our Heroku apps started to return the timeout error in Russia. 
Here is what we know so far:

1. All of our Heroku apps are affected
2. Users trying to reach them from Russia get time-out error
3. Users in Russia reach our apps just fine if using VPN
4. The issue affects only Heroku custom domains. For example billing.chaos-control.mobi is not reachable while chaos-control-billing.herokuapp.com is reachable. Both are urls for the chaos-control-billing app
5. DNS is set up properly (we already been through this with both Heroku and PointDNS support)

Heroku support suggested using QuotaGuard as a workaround. Please see what they said below.
P.S. I just realised your answered in the Heroku ticket. Should we proceed communicating there or via email?

Thank you for your help!
Dmitriy

Hi,
Thanks for providing that info and sorry for the delayed response. As far as I can tell, it looks like that domain is set up correctly. Unfortunately, we've had other reports of Russian origins having networking issues with Heroku. Due to the nature of the Heroku platform, this is difficult to rectify. Heroku apps have dynamic IP addressing. I've seen other engineers give the following solutions as possible workarounds:
  • The first is an add-on such as QuotaGuard Static (https://elements.heroku.com/addons/quotaguardstatic), that can provide an inbound proxy for your requests, however this may be prohibitively expensive depending on your traffic.
  • The second is to use a service such as Cloudflare, in order to act as a proxy between your users and the application, so requests terminate on Cloudflare's end.
  • The third option is to run a reverse proxy that is hosted outside of Heroku, so requests are proxied through that in order to get around the IP block from Roskomnadzor.

subject: qgtunnel installation instructions
description:
Hello, when we needed to install QGPass we received the instructions below, inclusive a download link for QGPass.  Do you have the same available for QGTunnel?
 
1. Download QGPass

Download and extract the qgpass in the root directory of your app:

 curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgpass-latest.tar.gz | tar xz 

2. Change your code

Change your request code (Tesla) to connect through QGPass at http://localhost:8080.
 
It looks like only the Mint adapter for Tesla supports HTTP proxies: https://hexdocs.pm/tesla/Tesla.Adapter.Mint.html
 
The Gun adapter only supports SOCKS proxies.
 
Let me know if that is an issue, we can look for alternatives if so.
​ 
 3. Change your startup code.
Change the code that starts up your application.  In gigalixir this is done through a Procfile.

So for a Procfile that was previously:
web: your-application your arguments
you would now want:
 web: bin/qgpass your-application your arguments

subject: Issues connecting to Postgres
description:
Hello!

I’m having issues connecting to an Azure Managed Postgres instance through QuotaGuard.

Here are the logs from QGTunnel when I attempt to proxy PSQL

2023/02/23 10:55:45 Version: 2.5.1
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Created proxy dialer for https://***@us-east-shield-03.quotaguard.com:9294
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Found tunnel configuration {"Tunnels":{"Fresh_Connect_Dev_Database":{"accept":"127.0.0.1:5432","connect":"freshconnect-dev.postgres.database.azure.com:5432","transparent":true,"encrypted":false}}}
2023/02/23 10:55:45 DNS Mode: DEFAULT
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Added DNS override for freshconnect-dev.postgres.database.azure.com:5432
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Starting listener on 127.0.0.1:5432 for freshconnect-dev.postgres.database.azure.com:5432
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Dynamic tunneling feature not enabled
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Finished initialization
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Starting new process /opt/homebrew/bin/psql with args: [psql ***]
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Started process. Waiting for it to exit
2023/02/23 10:55:45 Got new connection from 127.0.0.1:60246

I whitelisted the QG ips as well as my local IP. I can connect to the database fine with QGTunnel, but with QGTunnel the connect times out.

Here is my .qgtunnel file

[qgtunnel.Fresh_Connect_Dev_Database]
accept = "127.0.0.1:5432"
connect = "freshconnect-dev.postgres.database.azure.com:5432"
encrypted = false
transparent = true

Also I can only get QGTunnel to attempt to proxy the request when I set the hostname to localhost, instead of my azure database host, even though I’m running in transparency mode. When I use the Azure database host it doesn’t connect to QGTunnel.

I’m having issues connecting on both Mac and Debian.

Any thoughts on what could be going wrong?

Thanks!
Steve

import _ from 'lodash';

description:
We've exchanged a few emails back and forth and I wanted to put this conversation into Support so we can track getting it resolved. 

Original Steps: 
  1. Setup without the proxy first -> Done
  2. Attempt to run the same requests through the QG proxy -> Not working, so creating this ticket...
From Dean on Jan 20th: 

The app is working without the QuotaGuard installed and I already send the code to you. Here it is again:

import config
import json
from binance.client import Client
from binance.enums import *
from flask import Flask, request, render_template


app = Flask(__name__)

client = Client(config.API_KEY, config.API_SECRET, tld='com')


def order(side, quantity, symbol, order_type=ORDER_TYPE_MARKET):
    try:
        print(f"sending order {order_type} - {side} {quantity} {symbol}")
        order = client.futures_create_order(symbol=symbol, side=side, type=order_type, quantity=quantity)
    except Exception as e:
        print("an exception occurred - {}".format(e))
        return False

    return order


@app.route('/')
def welcome():
    return render_template('index.html')

@app.route('/webhook', methods=['POST'])
def webhook():

    data = json.loads(request.data)
    
    if data['passphrase'] != config.WEBHOOK_PASSPHRASE:
        return {
            "code": "error",
            "message": "Nice try, invalid passphrase"
        }

    side = data['strategy']['order_action'].upper()
    quantity = data['strategy']['order_contracts']
    symbol = data['ticker'].upper()
    order_response = order(side, quantity, symbol)

    if order_response:
        return {
            "code": "success",
            "message": "order executed"
        }
    else:
        print("order failed")

        return {
            "code": "error",
            "message": "order failed"
        }

Message: Hi,

We use QuotaGuard when making requests to people's SQL servers, so that they can whitelist the IP at the network level.

One customer has noticed that things stopped working when they put an AWS Network Load Balancer in front of their database. They report that they are able to use the database with the psql command-line tool, and with the Google Colab notework environment.

With QuotaGuard, a first connection works, but subsequent connections seem to time out.

We don't observe this issue when interacting with other databases.

We think something about QuotaGuard may be interacting with their NLB.

Can you help debug this?

A (very naive) test with curl demonstrates the problem.

Obviously curl isn't a postgres client, but it talks SOCKS and demonstrates the issue.

If we try to use QG against a vanilla postgres database, we can repeatedly run the following curl command and get responses. (They're errors, because, yes, curl isn't a psql client):

curl -v --proxy http://username:password@us-east-static-09-b.quotaguard.com:9293 http://dpg-bvnq1rblc6cpc67fjong.oregon-postgres.render.com:5432

Whereas if we run it aginst the client's NLB, the first connection will succeed, and then the rest will timeout. After some time, a connection will succeed again, and then timeout again.

curl -v --proxy http://user:pass@us-east-static-09-b.quotaguard.com:9293 http://public-nlb-for-private-databases-f38ef25ad4bde78a.elb.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com:5432

Thanks for any light you can shed!

subject: static IP for whitelisting on heroku
description:
Hi there,

I have a Heroku app (radconsult.ca), which needs to be used in an environment where only certain whitelisted IP addresses are accessible from a web-browser.

Our problem is that the heroku website where our domain points (https://rad-request.herokuapp.com/) does not have a static IP address.

Unfortunately, the whitelisting is only based on IP address - it can't be based on URL.  So every week or two, the website access fails, as the IP address changes.

I've been looking at your product, and it would seem to be a good fit.  Our traffic is minimal - it is essentially an internal web-app used by a dozen people or so.  If we enrol with the Startup Static or Shield option, would our URL be successfully registered as having one of your static IPs, for the purposes of whitelisting?

There's another note on your instructions, that static IPs for inbound traffic are only available at Micro plans or higher.  Not sure how this reconciles with other statements saying you provide static IP addresses at all levels.

Thanks in advance for the help!

Jon

Is it possible to use your addon with UDP protocol for inbound/outbound communication?
If not, it is feasible for you to add that functionality to your addon?

Many thanks
Ing. David Tosner
Factorio solutions, s.r.o

Thanks for reaching out and we can help fix this Heroku issue.

Starting November 28, 2022, Heroku eliminated their free product plans and started shutting down free dynos and data services. As such, Heroku removed all free dynos, hobby-dev Heroku Postgres and hobby-dev Heroku Data for Redis plans.

Two Options to Resume QuotaGuard Service

   1) QuotaGuard Direct Service - QuotaGuard does not require a Heroku dyno to operate, we work with all cloud providers, as well as, independently. To eliminate the need to pay for additional Heroku dynos, you can sign up with QuotaGuard directly and get the exact same plan, proxy, IP’s and cost.
       
     A) Navigate to our QuotaGuard Pricing Page.

     B) Sign up for the same service (QG Static or QG Shield) that you had on Heroku and the same payment plan.

     C) Email us at support@quotaguard.com letting us know you’ve signed up. We should be able to look up your prior proxy and move your new service to the same proxy/IP addresses.

               Information we need to look up your prior account (at least one data point should work):
               1) Prior QuotaGuard Username (Should look something like “nfinuf2872n8”)
               2) Email Address of a Heroku user for the app.

     D) We’ll email you back immediately that we’ve made the above change and you are ready to rebuild your connection.

          - Since this is a new subscription, retrieve the new connection string URL from your QuotaGuard Account.

      E) Setup your inbound or outbound connection, upload your certificates, and if you have any questions or issues, write us for help at support@quotaguard.com.

  2) Subscribe to Heroku Eco Dyno Plans - Heroku recently announced a new Eco dyno plan and Mini plan for Heroku Postgres and Heroku Data for Redis® that sleeps when not in use.

       A) Once signing up for a new plan on Heroku, Email us at support@quotaguard.com letting us know your app is back online. We should be able to look up your prior proxy and move your new service to the same proxy/IP addresses.

               Information we need to look up your prior account (at least one data point should work):
               1) Prior QuotaGuard Username (Should look something like “nfinuf2872n8”)

      E) Setup your inbound or outbound connection, upload your certificates, and if you have any questions or issues, write us for help at support@quotaguard.com.

I know this is all annoying and frustrating, but I hope this helps get you started to resolve your issues with Heroku.

We’re here all day and our schedules are clear so we can help, as we knew today would be a busy one. Just write us any time at support@quotaguard.com for help.

Michael

subject: Configuration question
description:
Hello!

I have an Elixir application that I’m setting up in fly.io, and I need to connect directly to an Azure SQL database running in Azure. I’d like to limit the SQL access to a specific set of IP addresses, which is why I’m trying to set up QuotaGuard. I _think_ I could use your qgtunnel download to get this done, but I was looking at installing Dante directly in my docker container… I have installed dante-client and dante-server via apt, and I’m trying to test connectivity using socks.conf with:


SOCKS_CONF=/usr/local/etc/socks.conf SOCKS_USERNAME=my-username SOCKS_PASSWORD=my-password socksify curl https://ifconfig.me

# /usr/local/etc/socks.conf
route {
        from: 0.0.0.0/0   to: 0.0.0.0/0   via: us-west-shield-01.quotaguard.com port = 9294
        protocol: tcp udp
        proxyprotocol: socks_v5
        method: username
}


When I run this, the curl hangs until it eventually times out at 5 minutes.

If I can get curl to work, but for some reason my Elixir application doesn’t pick up the proxy via LD_PRELOAD, I was considering setting up sockd instead on port 1080 and setting my database adapter to just point to localhost.

Anyways… I was wondering if you had any extra documentation for configuring Dante directly on a system, and if you had a hint of why my curl is failing. Is there a different hostname I should be using for socks proxies vs the config I got out of the QuotaGuard UI?

Thanks!
Eric

On Mon, Oct 31, 2022 at 2:42 PM Michael Crown <support@quotaguard.com> wrote:
Hi Tim,
​
  Thanks for the note and a couple easy answers below: 
​
  1) Need to upgrade?: Not this month, you are ok. 
 
   Like you mentioned, it's the last day of the month and I completely understand that it can be challenging to be just slightly above the limits. I'm not strict in that manner as the month closes out and subscriptions nudge about their billing. 
​
   All suspensions are only done by me after personal review and multiple attempts to contact the customer. In this case, you are just fine for October.
​
   If you think you'll use a simliar amount for next month, I'd recommend upgrading, as we don't like to see multiple months in a row of overage usage, but we can chat that out over email if you have some questions about whether that'll be a problem going forward. 
​
  2) Do IP's change? : Also no, they don't change when you upgrade. I touch on that a little bit here with What Happens When We Change Plans. 

  I hope that helps relieves any stress over October! 

  Let me know if you have any more questions of want to talk about usage for November. 
  
  Have a great week and chat soon,

Michael

description:
Hello,

Running "bin/qgtunnel echo test" using the following .qgtunnel file on a Docker image ubuntu:focal-20211006:

[qgtunnel.0]
accept = "127.0.0.1:7875"
connect = "rt1.ec2.dxfeed.com:7875"
encrypted = false
transparent = false

results in the following output:

ERROR: ld.so: object '/app/vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so' from LD_PRELOAD cannot be preloaded (cannot open shared object file): ignored.
test

but I understand that if transparent is set to false, this library is not required to be present. I also don't observe this behaviour on the Docker image alpine:3.15.3 - it appears to only be present on Ubuntu

What environment and configuration should I have to resolve this unnecessary log line? (it interferes with some Python version detection a third party library performs)

Thanks,
Matt

First of all, welcome to QuotaGuard Shield, we're happy you've decided to try out our service for your celeri-rails-staging application. This email should get you up and running in no time.
Please keep this email for future reference, as it can help with setting up, reaching out to support, knowing your configurations, and answering general FAQ.

Accessing Static IP Connection Settings

You can start using our service immediately using the credentials we added to your dyno in the QUOTAGUARDSHIELD_URL environment variable.
Additionally, your Static IP connection information can be found in your QuotaGuard administrator dashboard.
To reach the dashboard, either run $ heroku addons:open quotaguardshield or click on the upper right arrow next to the QuotaGuard Add­on. If you have trouble finding it, please follow Step 6 from the instructions in this blog post, How to Provision the QuotaGuard Add-on.

subject: Migrating from Heroku add-on to stand alone Quotaguard account
description:
Hello,

I have been communicating with your support team last year about moving the billing of a Heroku add-on to another Heroku app without losing the 2 static IPs we had. You provided me with a good solution but the project never got priority and never happened. Here is the original conversation: https://help.heroku.com/tickets/1040883

Today I'm revisiting this project, and I think it would be much simpler for us to open an account directly with you instead of going through Heroku add-ons. Could you confirm if the following assumptions are possible before I subscribe a Medium plan please?

1) Migrate env vars from QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL to QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_MANUAL_URL as described in original plan.
2) Create an account directly on Quotaguard.
3) Ask Quotaguard to set our static IPs to the same values as before (52.5.238.209 and 52.6.13.167). Subscribe to Medium plan (100000 requests / month for $49)
3) On staging, change QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_MANUAL_URL value to the URL provided from the new Quotaguard account. Confirm everything works fine.
4) Repeat the same step for production.
5) Once normal operation is confirmed, remove the Heroku add-ons and remove QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL env var.

Kind regards,
Jeremy Marin

Thanks!

-Ben

Thanks,
Kaiyi

subject: Connecting to SQL Server through QuotaGuardShield
description:
To whom it may concern:
 
We have an QuotaGuardShield add-on provisioned with a Heroku App.
 
Our subscription support code is: qgverify-fd9453bc-f7c3-4a4d-a19a-43547ddf4cff
 
Problem/need:
  • We are trying to connect to a SQL Server database hosted in AWS from our Heroku App
  • So this is NOT any kind of HTTPS, web page, requests. It’s purely trying to connect to a SQL Server DB hosted on an AWS server, from our Heroku App (using Apache, PHP).
 
Things we’ve done/tried so far:
  • The host of the db is on an AWS server – aka ec2-<xxx-xxx-xx-xx>.computer-<x>.amazonaws.com
  • We have opened the firewall hosting the SQL Server db to our 2 IP addresses assigned by QG
  • We opened port 1433 for those IPs, and 1434
 
  • We use the .qgtunnel setup – we use environmental variables (Heroku Settings) to define the host to connect to
    • We use transparent mode
    • We verified the remote host is the correct one (at least what we think is being exposed to our Heroku App)
    • We tried connecting to 127.0.0.1 as well.
 
Results we are seeing:
  • SQLSTATE: HYT00
  • code: 0
  • message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]Login timeout expired
  • SQLSTATE: 08001
  • code: 258
  • message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]TCP Provider: Error code 0x102
  • SQLSTATE: 08001
  • code: 258
  • message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]A network-related or instance-specific error has occurred while establishing a connection to SQL Server. Server is not found or not accessible. Check if instance name is correct and if SQL Server is configured to allow remote connections. For more information see SQL Server Books Online.
  • host attempted - <<dns name redacted…. Is it insecure to send that in an email???>>,1433
 
When we try to use 127.0.0.1,143 (which was set up for using transparent mode), we get this:
  • SQLSTATE: HYT00
  • code: 0
  • message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]Login timeout expired
  • SQLSTATE: 08001
  • code: 258
  • message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]TCP Provider: Timeout error [258].
  • SQLSTATE: 08001
  • code: 258
  • message: [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server]Unable to complete login process due to delay in prelogin response
  • host attempted - 127.0.0.1,1433
 
We have tried encryption true and false (but not sure we have used with all possible combinations).
 
I believe we have configured QuotaGuardShield (and the qgtunnel) correctly because we also did this:
  • In our Heroku App we provisioned a small SQL Server DB
  • I obtained the host/connection credentials of that
  • I set up a qgtunnel to with that info
  • I was able to login and query data of that SQL Server instance – in fact, I saw on the Dashboard the couple requests and data transfer that occurred
 
I understand you all are not obligated to solve every customer’s SQL Server/hosting dilemmas, but I’m hoping you have a few quick pointers.
 
Any thoughts and suggestions are greatly appreciated.
 
Best,
-Charlie Coleman
 
CHARLES COLEMAN
Software Developer

setup:

build:

RUN apk add curl

Error relocating /go/vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so: __register_atfork: symbol not found

Is there a copy of gqtunnel for MacOS that I could test locally without a container? Could there be a missing file within the golang alpine image?

Thank you for your time.
-Michael

Getting Started With QuotaGuard.com

Hi,
First of all, welcome to QuotaGuard Static, we're happy you've decided to try out our service for your uplisting-worker-production application. This email should get you up and running in no time.
Please keep this email for future reference, as it can help with setting up, reaching out to support, knowing your configurations, and answering general FAQ.

Accessing Static IP Connection Settings

You can start using our service immediately using the credentials we added to your dyno in the QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL environment variable.
Additionally, your Static IP connection information can be found in your QuotaGuard administrator dashboard.
To reach the dashboard, either run $ heroku addons:open quotaguardstatic or click on the upper right arrow next to the QuotaGuard Add­on. If you have trouble finding it, please follow Step 6 from the instructions in this blog post, How to Provision the QuotaGuard Add-on.

Your Static IPs

  • 3.250.252.133
  • 63.32.41.221
Please allow all IP addresses for any whitelisting or firewall rules, as traffic may route through any of the IP addresses at any time.

Subscription Information

Username: 6jcemxxk0c0d2h
Proxy Password: Located in your dashboard

Connection Strings

HTTP url: http://6jcemxxk0c0d2h:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-static-05.quotaguard.com:9293 (for HTTP and HTTPS traffic)
SOCKS url: socks5://6jcemxxk0c0d2h:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-static-05.quotaguard.com:1080 (for all types of TCP traffic)

Testing Your Connection

via Heroku CLI

$ heroku run 'curl -x http://6jcemxxk0c0d2h:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-static-05.quotaguard.com:9293 -L ip.quotaguard.com'

via Curl

$ curl -x http://6jcemxxk0c0d2h:{PASSWORD}@eu-west-static-05.quotaguard.com:9293 -L ip.quotaguard.com

Inbound Proxy

Setup instructions for Inbound Proxy's and Custom Domains can be found at Getting Started with QuotaGuard's Static IP Inbound Proxy.

Support

To access support and get help, we have a few options for you, or you can just open a new ticket at our Support portal and we will answer you directly.
  • Heroku Documentation for QuotaGuard Static.
  • Setup Support for configuring with Node.js, Ruby, Python, Go, Java, and PHP, etc.
  • Setup QuotaGuard for MongoDB
  • Need to Create a Support Ticket?
  • News and Announcements? Find them at our Blog
  • Request for Dedicated Proxy Setup (Enterprise plans and higher)
  • Do you have Privacy, GDPR, or Legal Questions?
Thanks for giving us a try and don't be shy about reaching out for help, we're always here to assist with any questions you might have.
Michael
QuotaGuard Static
P.S. If you are working with sensitive data like HIPAA, Financial, or Personally Identifiable Information (PII), you will want to check out QuotaGuard Shield. It's the same as QuotaGuard Static but with stronger end to end security for your requests.

Claim your free $10 Amazon Gift Card when you Share How You Found Us

We are always interested to learn how you came to subscribe to QuotaGuard Static. If you don’t mind, we would love to hear about how you found our service. Just reply to this email, tell us where you heard about QuotaGuard and we will mail you a $10 Amazon Gift Card as a thank you for your feedback. Limit 1 per subscription.

description:
Hi there,

Our company is going to use QuotaGuard Shield, but we faced one issue with our Ruby app.
When we try to perform this code from the Ruby on Rails app, we always receive a timeout error "RestClient::Exceptions::ReadTimeout (Timed out reading data from server)". 
This code is correct, because it's from QuotaGuard docs.
require 'rest-client'

RestClient.proxy = ENV['QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL'] if ENV['QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL']

res = RestClient.get('http://ip.jsontest.com')

puts "Your IP was: #{res.body}"
I tried other libraries like Faraday, Excon and NET:HTTP and it always doesn't work.

At the same time, I tested QuotaGuard with another account with Static Micro plan, and it works ok.
Can you please help me to understand what can be wrong with the QuotaGuard Shield and Ruby on Rails application?

Thanks,
Iren Liber

subject: Issues making connection via Quotaguard IP in background worker
description:
Hello,
 
In our Rails app running in Heroku using Quotaguard, I am attempting to configure a background job that establishes a connection to a separate Postgres server via our Quotaguard dedicated IP. I have the connection working properly in Rails console (when I run it via `heroku run bin/qgsocksify rails c`) but when I modify our app Procfile to launch workers via `bin/qgsocksify bundle exec sidekiq -C ./config/sidekiq.yml` and try running a test worker that establishes the connection, the worker just appears to hang (other workers are unaffected and run normally).
 
The DB connection is being established via: `ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection Rails.configuration.mitchells_postgres_database`
 
I suspect that the connection the worker is attempting to establish is not coming over our QG IP, even though the PG URL has been added to QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_MASK and the connection is working via Rails console. Is there a recommended way of establishing a connection via QG IP from a worker/non-web Heroku process?
 
Our Heroku app name is mitchellstores-demo. Thanks for your help!
 
Eric

subject: Dropped connections
description:
Hi,

We’re in the process of moving to QuotaGuard — we point our DNS at QuotaGuard Shield and send our inbound traffic through it but point it back to us (through Heroku) directly when we find that there’s an issue.

Most recently, we re-enabled QuotaGuard Shield on December 6, and then on December 7, we found that although we did not have any issues with our own site, our request throughput was going way down, in a spiky fashion. See the attached image. Seeing this and connecting it to the recent re-enabling of QuotaGuard, we pointed our DNS back at Heroku directly and the issue went away.

I know that there were issues with AWS that day, but I’m not sure if that’s related or not. Either way, one thing that’s concerning is that we did not see any alerts about this. Do you have any insight into why this may have happened? And secondly, if this were to happen again in the future, is there some sort of alerting mechanism?

Best,
Rudd Zwolinski
Engineering Director, Zearn

out-app ---1 --> static-proxy -- 2 --> external service

If we would talk directly with the external service like

out-app --- 3 --> external service

Tomaz

{

The DNS Target needs to be the DNS target provided by heroku when you setup the Custom Domain (ie: www.mydomain.com) in the heroku dashboard.

Let me know if you have any questions,
Tim

description:
Hi QuotaGuard Support,

We are using QGTunnel and want to understand how to make use of the QGTUNNEL_CONFIG environment variable, instead of relying on the dashboard to download the tunnel configuration (we've been receiving the reminder emails as well).

I've been reading this:
https://blog.quotaguard.com/store-individual-environment-variables-in-qgtunnel-environment-variable/
and this:
https://quotaguard.github.io/qg-docs/how-do-i-set-up-environment-specific-qgtunnel-files.html

First one says: Therefore, in an effort to make this easier for everyone, we’ve added the ability to store the path to that configuration file in a new environment variable “QGTUNNEL_CONFIG”. which seems to refer to storing the path of the file.

Second article says: You can download your configuration from the QG Dashboard and store it in an application environment variable “QGTUNNEL_CONFIG”.
Does it mean the same as the first one, or does it mean having the actual configuration sotred in the environment variable? The latter would actually be preferable - in case of tunnel configuration changes, changing the environment variable is a lot easier/quicker as opposed to updating code repository and deploying new code in Heroku.

Can you confirm if we can store the config directly to the environment variable?
And if yes, the .qgtunnel contents are in the format like below, so we just use that whole multi-line string as the value of the environment variable?
[qgtunnel.0]
accept = "127.0.0.1:1234"
connect = "ec2-00-00-00-00.eu-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com:1234"
encrypted = false
transparent = true

I plan to carry out some testing too, but thought to reach out for clarification.

Thanks,
Arnold Manzano

subject: QuotaGuard Setup
description:
Hi,

We will shortly be launching QuotaGuard Static Shield for our application Dent on Heroku (quotaguardshield-lively-10760, mrj477farivxbv, not sure what other identifier might be helpful). We recently got the dedicated proxy set up and are about to start using it. i just had a few questions to help the process go smoothly.

Our plan is that we will be setting up an inbound proxy such that all requests to our application will be going through QuotaGuard. Our app is hosted at www.zearn.org. We also have the bare domain zearn.org redirect to the www version; that’s currently automatically set up in Heroku. Would you recommend we set up two inbound proxies, one for www and one for without? Or would you recommend only setting www to go through QuotaGuard? Note that our DNS provider is dnsimple. For the www subdomain we currently use a CNAME, and for the bare domain we use an ALIAS record that also goes to Heroku. Your inbound proxy directions within your app only mention using CNAMEs, even when I enter in the bare domain for an inbound proxy. I think ALIAS should work the same but I’m not 100% sure.

Also, many years ago, we used zearn.com instead of .org. I’m sure those don’t get much traffic anymore, but right now those (both www and bare) are set up within Heroku to also forward to www.zearn.org. I think these could probably continue to go only through Heroku. Is that what you would recommend?

When setting these up, once we have set up the inbound proxy (or proxies), all we need to do is set our DNS to point to the right inbound proxy URLs, and nothing else needs to be done, right?

Finally, is there any use to the QUOTAGUARDSHIELD_URL set up within our Heroku config vars?

Thanks in advance,
Rudd Zwolinski
Engineering Director, Zearn

description:
Hi there,

Here’s my use-case. I have an app on Heroku and need to connect to an LDAP-server via a static IP.
I added the QuotaGuard addon and saw that I can use the QGTunnel-script.

- the ldap://-protocol is replaced with tcp:// on the tunnel.
- all outgoing traffic is proxied (including the traffic to the postgresql-dababase, which uses a different port, and now is inaccessible, unless I add a tunnel for that too).

Can you please take a look at these two concerns.
I thought the QGTunnel would only ‘tunnel’ requests that actually use a tunnel, and ignore the rest.

Thanks in advance for your reply,

subject: Unable to send outbound traffic with static IP
description:
Hi,

I am a Ruby on Rails developer and I had implemented block.io API in my project.
This API requires setting the 'API key access' restricted for specific IP addresses for the block.io user.
I had earlier set the IP address of our Heroku instance in the setting, but the API didn't allow its access as the IP address of Heroku had changed.
The IP addresses of Heroku are dynamic, so I used the add-on 'QuotaGuardStatic' to get the static IPs, and access the API using this static IP.

I have implemented the add-on as mentioned in QuotaGuardStatic documentation (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/quotaguardstatic) and set the outbound 'http proxy with Ruby/Rails'.
I have followed these steps:-
1. heroku addons:create quotaguardstatic:starter
2. heroku config:get QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL
3. set http proxy using RestClient
require "rest-client"

RestClient.proxy = ENV["QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL"]

res = RestClient.get("http://ip.quotaguard.com")

puts "Your Static IP is: #{res.body}"

This is returning the Static IP (Please see the attachment), but the outbound traffic is still using the dynamic one (when calling block.io API) and not the static ones that the add-on has provided.

Can you please provide the solution to this?

Hi Michael,

I'm afraid it is as I expected.  However, you can work around it with our QGPass program. 

QGPass is a wrapper program that makes using the the HTTPS Proxy as easy as connecting to an unauthenticated HTTP Proxy.  Connection can be made to localhost:8080 with no credentials, then QGPass will use the secure HTTPS connection URL to proxy your requests through our proxy servers.

Here are the instructions I would use to get QGPass up and running:

1. Download QGPass

Download and extract the qgpass in the root directory of your app:
​
For linux:
 curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgpass-latest.tar.gz | tar xz 
​
For mac:
 curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgpass-1.1.0-darwin.tar.gz | tar xz 
​
For windows, download from here and unzip:  https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgpass-1.1.0.zip
​
2.  Setup the environment variable

Setup the environment variable QUOTAGUARDSHIELD_URL to be equal to your Connection URL in the Setup page of our dashboard.

3. Start postman with QGpass
​
./bin/qgpass Postman
​
5. Update the proxy settings
Change your settings to connect through QGPass at http://localhost:8080.
 
​
Tim

From: Tim Day <staticsupport@quotaguard.com>
Sent: Wednesday, September 8, 2021 08:18
To: Charlie Bini <CBini@kippteamandfamily.org>
Subject: Re: PythonAnywhere guide with MSSQL?
 
Hi Charlie,
 
Unfortunately Python's MSSQL implementations are extrapolations of C libraries and there is no clean way to insert a proxy directly into the implementation.  So QGTunnel is the best bet.  The setup is very similar to MySQL, just with different ports involved.  I have included the directions below for reference.
Tim
 I suggest you go with the SOCKS proxy using our QGTunnel software.  Here are some setup instruction to get you started:
 
1. Download QGTunnel into the root of your project
 
 curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/quotaguard/qgtunnel-latest.tar.gz | tar xz  
 
 
 
2. Log in to our dashboard and setup the tunnel
 
Once you are logged into our dashboard, in the top right menu, go to Setup (Gear Icon), click on QGTunnel Configuration, then Create Tunnel.
 
 
Remote Destination: tcp://hostname.for.your.server.com:1433 
Local Port: 1433
Transparent: true
Encrypted: false
 
This setup assumes that the remote mssql server is located at hostname.for.your.server.com and is listening on port 1433.  This is usually the default port.
 
The Local Port is the port number that QGTunnel will listen on.  In this example we set it to 5432, but if you have another process using 1433, you may have to change it (ie: 1434).
 
Transparent mode allows QGTunnel to override the DNS for hostname.for.your.server.com to 127.0.0.1, which redirects traffic to the QGTunnel software.  This means you can connect to either hostname.for.your.server.com or 127.0.0.1 to connect through the tunnel.
 
Encrypted mode can be used to encrypt data end-to-end, but if your protocol is already encrypted then you don't need to spend time setting it up.  I believe mssql is already encrypted but you should double check.
 
 
 
3. Change your code to connect through the tunnel
With transparent mode and matching Local and Remote ports you should not need to change your code.  You can also connect to 127.0.0.1:1433.
 
Without transparent mode, you will want to connect to 127.0.0.1:1433.
 
 
 
4. Change your startup code.
Change the code that starts up your application.  In many platforms, this is done with a Procfile.  Basically you just need to prepend your startup code with "bin/qgtunnel".
 
So for a Procfile that was previously:
web: your-application your arguments
you would now want:
 web: bin/qgtunnel your-application your arguments  
 
 
 
5.  Setup the environment variable QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL to be equal to your Connection URL in the Setup page of our dashboard. 
 
If you added us from a cloud provider (azure, cloudfoundry, heroku, ibm cloud, pivotal, etc) then this is usually done for you.  Please note that QGTunnel handles converting the HTTP URL and port to the SOCKS5 URL and port.  So either of the connection URLs is fine.
 
 
 
6. Commit and push your code.
Be sure that the file  bin/qgtunnel  is added to your repository. 
 
If you are using transparent mode, be sure that  vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so  is also added to your repository.
 
If you are not using transparent mode, you will want to set the environment variable QGTUNNEL_DNSMODE to DISABLED to avoid seeing an error message in your logs.
 
7.  If you have problems, enable the environment variable  QGTUNNEL_DEBUG=true  and then restart your application while watching the logs.  Send me any information in the logs. Please redact any sensitive information, including your QuotaGuard connection URL.
 
 
VERY IMPORTANT
8. After you get everything working, I suggest you download your QGTunnel configuration from our dashboard as a  .qgtunnel  file and put that in the root of your project.  This prevents your project from relying on our website during startup.
 
Alternatively you can put the contents of the downloaded configuration file in a QGTUNNEL_CONFIG environment variable.

subject: Static IP - question around pricing plan
description:
Hi QuotaGuard,
 
I am looking to implement a simple Rails app for an Australian University. I want to use Rack::Attack to restrict the app to users who are either on-prem or VPN.
Due to the way the University’s VPN is configured, I would like to use QuotaGuard to give the app a Static IP (or small range of known IPs) so that it can be added to their VPN configuration.
 
This app will have very little traffic as it is to be used internally by the testing team. Would we be able to use the Micro or similar plan to achieve this objective? I noticed that “Dedicated IP addresses” are only available on the Enterprise plan, which would be a hard sell to the Infra team cost wise. The app would be fine with a known range of inbound IP addresses, assuming the list was relatively constrained.
 
Can you please let me know if the Micro/Medium plan would be ok, or if we would need to try and go with the Enterprise plan? Happy to provide further details as needed. Thank you.
 
 
Regards,
Nik Bagdon | Cloud Architect
Identifly Pty Ltd | Adelaide, South Australia

subject: Laravel app is not connecting with QG tunnel.
description:
Hey Team, I hope you are all doing well. 

Recently I configured qgtunnel with Ruby on Rails and I was able to make it work for the SOCKS5 proxy. I was able to connect my remote AWS DB with static IP's provided by Quotaguard.

But now im trying to configure it with one of my Laravel's App. and looks like my qgtunnel is not connecting. Please let me know what i'm missing here, I have followed all the instructions very preciesly that's how I was able to configure it for ROR, now i'm following same instructions for Laravel and its not woring.

This is the Procfile I used for ROR which is working fine, I had to inlcude unicorn.rb file btw:

web: bin/qgtunnel bundle exec unicorn -p $PORT -c ./config/unicorn.rb

This is the Procfile i'm using for Laravel, but it's not woring;

web: bin/qgtunnel vendor/bin/heroku-php-apache2 public/

Regards,
Sadique

Getting Started With QuotaGuard.com

Thanks for giving us a try and don't be shy about reaching out for help, we're always here to assist with any questions you might have.

Just on a note, we investigated every other system and everything seems fine with the rest of our tech stack. The attached graphs are for two of the services using QuotaGuard to communicate with 3rd parties.

Regards, 
Marco

description:
Hi Guys,

I’m on the free plan here, but I’m hoping you can help me out. (If we can get this to work we will be signing up with you on a number of reasonably active application instances.)

I’m having trouble connecting via the tunnel to my AWS RDS MySQL instance from my Rails app.

Here’s the config

QuotaGuard username: s889h1n8yzaq8h

- Procfile:
web: bin/qgtunnel bundle exec puma -C config/puma.rb
worker: bin/qgtunnel bundle exec sidekiq -C config/sidekiq.yml
scheduler: bin/qgtunnel bundle exec clockwork clock.rb

- bin/qgtunnel and /vendor/nss_wrapper/libnss_wrapper.so are present / checked in.

subject: Unable to connect to postgres database
description:
Hello Michael,
I am having problems connecting  to a Postgres database server  from a container running .Net in Heroku. This is my app setup.
 
Dentally-wlapi-draft is a container running a .Net app. This container successfully deployed to Heroku and I can ping it to verify it is responding.
The Postgres database server is running on Amazon RDS with a base domain of rds.amazonaws.com and port 5432.
QGTunnel was configured to listen on the db server host and port.
               
The connection details have been verified outside the app.
The qgtunnel tar file was downloaded and added to the container (I don’t’ have curl in the container). The tar was extracted and I confirmed there is bin/ and vendor/ folders in the same folder as my app’s dll.
The .qgtunnel configuration has been added to the same folder as the app’s dll.
The IP addresses (both of them) under QuotaGuard connection info have been whitelisted in the appropriate AWS area.
 
When I run a command on the app that attempts to access the postgres db, the connection times out.
2021-05-05T21:54:50.826281+00:00 app[web.1]: Npgsql.NpgsqlException (0x80004005): Exception while connecting
2021-05-05T21:54:50.826282+00:00 app[web.1]: ---> System.TimeoutException: Timeout during connection attempt
2021-05-05T21:54:50.826766+00:00 app[web.1]: at Npgsql.NpgsqlConnector.Connect(NpgsqlTimeout timeout)
 
This is the same error I was getting before setting up QuotaGuard. I set up QG because I believed the problem lay in Heroku ip addresses being blocked.
 
I am not sure what else needs to be done. QGTunnel was supposed to work without changing the code (I’d rather not have to change the code).
 
Any help and guidance is appreciated.
 
Thank you.
Ernest

subject: Need help setting up SOCKS5 with Heroku: Java application
description:
Hello!
I am an IT student from Ukraine. We've been assigned to write a simple messenger app and deploy it on a remote server.
I am totally new to web technologies, having a background only in simple desktop apps on C++, C# and Python.
Right now I am writing the server-side code for the messenger using sockets on Java!

Since Heroku does not provide us with a static IP which is required for the type of app I want to make, the solution was obvious: QuotaGuard. I chose SOCKS5 because this is a desktop application, so I want to use TCP/IP, not HTTP/HTTPS.
Let's get to the point!
 I have configured my tunnel to run on https://mojimoji-server.herokuapp.com:80 — mojimoji-server being the name of my app on Heroku, and 80 being a number which I saw in a Heroku FAQ once, though I am not sure if the port should be 80. I've configured my local port to 8087 which is always open on my local machine.

I have a number of questions:
1. Which ports should I use for the value that goes after ...herokuapp.com: and my local port in the tunnel configuration? Shouldn't ports be read from the Heroku environment variable $PORT?
2. Which IP do I connect to once the app is deployed and is using tunnelling? Since QuotaGuard SOCKS5 grants my app a static IP address, where can I see it?

I would greatly appreciate it if you answered my questions. This is my first time deploying an app on a server — there are far more questions than answers. Thanks for your attention! :)
